questions.q: On solara-train, which interconnect provides the highest bandwidth between two GPUs?
options: InfiniBand NDR, if the two GPUs are on the same node
NVLink, if the two GPUs are on the same node
NVLink, regardless of which nodes the GPUs are on
Standard Ethernet
questions.explain: NVLink connects GPUs within the same node at up to 900 GB/s. GPUs on different nodes communicate over InfiniBand instead, which is slower than intra-node NVLink.

questions.q: In `nvidia-smi topo -m` output, what does a cell showing `NV18` between two GPUs indicate?
options: The two GPUs are not connected at all
The two GPUs are connected by 18 NVLink links
The two GPUs are on 18 different nodes
The GPU driver version is 18
questions.explain: The NV# notation in nvidia-smi topo -m indicates an NVLink connection with that many links between the two GPUs — a healthy, fast intra-node path.

questions.q: What does 'rail-optimized' describe in a cluster topology like solara-train's?
options: A cooling system for the GPU racks
A wiring scheme where each GPU index is wired to the same dedicated switch across every node
A type of NVLink cable
A Kubernetes scheduling policy
questions.explain: Rail-optimized topology assigns each GPU index (e.g., GPU 0 on every node) to its own dedicated switch/rail, so that cross-node traffic between matching GPU indices doesn't contend with traffic on other rails.

questions.q: Why does rail-optimized wiring specifically benefit NCCL's ring and tree collective algorithms?
options: Because those algorithms only work over Ethernet
Because those algorithms frequently move data between the same GPU index on different nodes, and rail-optimization gives that traffic a dedicated, uncontended switch
Because it eliminates the need for InfiniBand entirely
Because it increases NVLink bandwidth within a node
questions.explain: Ring and tree collectives move data between matching GPU indices across nodes very frequently; rail-optimized topology dedicates a switch to that exact traffic pattern, avoiding contention with other rails.

questions.q: What is the 'blast radius' of a single InfiniBand switch failure in a rail-optimized topology like solara-train's?
options: The entire 512-GPU cluster goes offline
Only the GPUs sharing that one rail across all nodes are affected
Nothing is affected because switches are redundant by default
Only one node's power supply is affected
questions.explain: Because each rail serves the same GPU index across every node, a single rail's switch failure affects only the GPUs on that one rail across all 64 nodes — not the entire cluster, but still a meaningful blast radius worth understanding.
